extracted.intended_audience: KAKENHI peer reviewers (academic reviewers for JSPS grants)
extracted.subtask_short: KAKENHI peer review for JSPS grants
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation guidance for peer reviewers who assess KAKENHI (Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research) proposals under JSPS, covering core rating elements, scoring, conflict rules, and review-stage procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic Importance of the Research Project
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate: Originality and novelty of the research question; Importance of the expected results to the academic field; Contribution to the development of the discipline; For "Generative Research Fields" categories: extent to which the project pioneers a new area; For "Challenging Research" categories: extent of explicit ambition to overturn established understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the research question is new and whether expected outcomes matter to the field. Pay attention to category-specific expectations (pioneering new areas for generative fields; explicit ambition to overturn understanding for challenging research). Consider contribution to disciplinary development rather than only technical detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of the Research Method
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate: Soundness of the proposed approach; Feasibility of the planned procedures; Appropriateness of methods to the research question; Plausibility of the timeline; Adequacy of preliminary results supporting the approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge methodological rigor and whether methods answer the research question within the proposed timeline and resources. Consider whether preliminary results sufficiently support feasibility and whether procedures are realistic and appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of the Ability to Conduct Research and the Research Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate: Demonstrated track record relevant to the project; Availability of facilities, equipment, materials, and resources; Composition and complementarity of the research team; Institutional embedding adequate to support the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the applicant(s)' prior accomplishments and whether the research environment (facilities, team composition, institutional support) makes successful execution likely. Look for complementary skills in the team and concrete institutional backing.

rubrics_metrics.name: No mechanical aggregation (reviewer discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: "No mechanical aggregation": reviewers are not required to give high scores to research proposals that marked high scores in all individual elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should exercise holistic judgment and may advance proposals that are unbalanced across elements if they are significant. Avoid strictly averaging element scores to determine merit; use discretion to weigh exceptional strengths or important trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of research is required to be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not converge on a single dominant model of "good" research; the system explicitly aims to fund a diverse portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When scoring or recommending, account for portfolio diversity goals. Do not unduly favor proposals that fit only one narrow conception of quality; consider varied approaches and topics to maintain a balanced funding portfolio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage document review procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-stage document review for most categories: each proposal is read independently in a first stage, then re-scored in a second stage where reviewers see the distribution of first-stage scores (without revealing other reviewers' identities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In first stage score independently. In second stage, re-evaluate in light of the anonymized distribution of first-stage scores; adjust scores as appropriate but respect anonymity. This procedural rule shapes how reviewers should approach initial and subsequent assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive review with panel deliberation (where applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive review for the largest categories (S/A, Challenging Research): reviewers conduct document reviews, then deliberate face-to-face in a panel that produces a synthesised assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For categories requiring comprehensive review, be prepared to discuss and defend assessments in panel meetings and to contribute to a synthesized panel judgment rather than only independent written scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring scales and verbal anchors
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rating element is scored on a 4- or 5-point scale (varies by category). Example verbal anchors (for Scientific Research (S)): 4: Should definitely be selected; 3: Better to select; 2: Hard to determine; 1: Difficult to select.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the category-specific scale and verbal anchors when assigning scores. Be mindful that scales differ by category (4- vs 5-point); use anchors to align numeric scores with qualitative judgments and to communicate recommendation strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest rules (must decline review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must decline if: They are at the same institution as the applicant; They have a co-authorship or supervisory relationship in recent years; They have a direct competitive interest in the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recuse yourself when institutional, collaborative, supervisory, or direct competitive relationships could bias judgment. Follow JSPS rules to avoid conflicts and maintain impartiality; err on the side of recusal when in doubt.
